answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce token stake before it may post jobs or claim payment, then slash that stake when a bonded counterparty proves fraud under a published dispute rule. Creating a thousand identities no longer multiplies influence for free: each needs capital, and colluding accounts risk losing it. A sonnet, velvet, or vine can decorate a profile, but none substitutes for collateral; the attacker pays an opportunity cost even if the fake identities are never caught.
